thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=decode-svc p99 latency spike detected in PROD (region=us-west-2). Start=2003456789. Auto-page sent to #eng-oncall.

alex: saw this around 16:02 UTC — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s, p99 to ~8–12s. Streaming sessions are stalling at token 512+ (lots of backpressure).

maria: confirmed — traces show long "kv cache page" IO spikes on GPU nodes, plus a noticeable bump right after a TRT + flashattn kernel push yesterday night.

kevin: CC @anya @ryan — can someone take lead? I'm on a deploy to fix another issue.

anya: taking lead. Gathering notes:
- Affected: decode-svc (all models using kernel=decode_kernel_v3, TRT 8.9.0, FlashAttention v2.1).
- Symptoms: streaming stalls, high tail latency on decode paths, paging I/O (nvlink swap?) for KV caches.
- Customer impact: intermittent fresh-user requests time out; degraded streaming UX for ~5% of traffic.

ryan: stack traces look like kernel compilepath is forcing larger temporary allocations when sequence length > 512; we see memory pressure leading to host-device transfers.

maria: reproducer on staging with model=redwood-small + seqlen=1024 reproduces p99 tail at ~6s after switching to decode_kernel_v3. Reverted to decode_kernel_v2 on staging and tail latency returned to baseline.

anya: initial mitigation plan: 1) start rolling rollback of decode_kernel_v3 on a small canary pool, 2) enable streaming fallback policy to CPU for active sessions over threshold, 3) pin compiler flags that changed in last build.

kevin: for rollback: use the orchestrator job ->
```
redwood-deploy rollback --service=decode-svc --pool=canary --image=decode_kernel_v2 --reason="latency spike"
```
I'll trigger after we confirm canary.

alex: quick check: are there any autoscaler thrash events? I see a flurry of pod restarts ~15:58 UTC but not correlated to CPU. Mostly OOM/kernel-killed on gpu nodes.

maria: logs from one failing pod:
```
[2026-03-14T15:59:12Z] ERROR decode: failed to allocate kv cache temp of 1.2GB -> host fallback; transfer took 3200ms
[2026-03-14T15:59:15Z] WARN  flashattn: workspace exceeded expected size; compiled kernels: decode_kernel_v3
```

anya: good evidence it's compilepath/kernel change. I'm going to open mitigation tickets and start rollback on canary. @ryan can you prepare the compiler-flag pin (build tag: COMPAT_PIN_20260314) so we can rebuild with old flags?

ryan: prepping. The flag diff included toggling -DUSE_FLASHATTN_V2 and enabling -O3_VECTORIZE that changed memory layout for temp buffers. I'll pin to previous commit and build a decode_kernel_v3-compat image. ETA ~25m.

incident-bot: Paging update: incident severity -> SEV2. SLO breach estimated for p99 in last 5m.

anya: rolling canary rollback now. Starting with 3 nodes in us-west-2-canary pool.

kevin: rolling. watch logs: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=decode-svc -c decode --follow`

maria: after first canary rollback: p95 back to ~150ms, p99 down to ~900ms on canary nodes. Good sign.

alex: pushing a temporary rule in the router to prefer decode_kernel_v2 for streaming routes to reduce exposure while we finish rollback: `route.override decode-svc:stream -> kernel:decode_kernel_v2`

anya: doing that now. Also enabling streaming fallback limit to 2s (was 5s) to reduce end-to-end stall visible to frontend.

kevin: note — need to notify SRE and Product because customers will see degraded streaming until fully rolled back.

maria: logged incident ticket: INC-20260314-42, included initial impact, mitigation steps, and reproducer. Adding metrics snapshot and traces.

ryan: compiler pin done and build triggered for decode_kernel_v3-compat. I'm adding build tag and disabling the -O3_VECTORIZE vectorization that changes workspace layout.

anya: timeline update: canary rollback 16:20–16:32, initial improvements. Plan: 1) finish node pool rollback across us-west-2 by 16:50, 2) roll remaining regions by 17:30 after verifying telemetry. If decode_kernel_v3-compat build passes tests, we'll redeploy compatible kernel and then re-run performance validation before re-enabling newer flags.

incident-bot: Update: SLO alert cleared for canary pool; global SLO still marginal.

alex: customer comms draft (short): "We observed a service regression impacting streaming latency due to a recent inference kernel update. We've rolled back the change for a portion of traffic and are deploying a fix. We will follow up with a detailed RCA." @maria pls iterate.

maria: sending now to comms, adding mitigation steps and ETA.

kevin: question — do we have a test for seqlen>512 memory layout? We should add a perf test gating kernels.

ryan: agreed. I'll add a new perf eval job that runs long-seq streaming scenarios and checks workspace allocations. Add as required check for kernel rollout.

anya: handoff: my oncall window ends in 40m. @alex you'll take primary after me; @maria keep owning comms. I'll leave a runbook in the incident ticket with steps to rollback, commands, and checks.

anya: runbook snippet:
```
# rollback canary
redwood-deploy rollback --service=decode-svc --pool=canary --image=decode_kernel_v2
# monitor
metrics query "p99(decode_svc_latency) by pool"
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=decode-svc -c decode --since=10m | grep "kv cache"
# pin router for streaming
route.override decode-svc:stream -> kernel:decode_kernel_v2
```

alex: taking over. I'll watch the remaining rollouts and validate p99 in 10m windows. Thanks @anya for triage.

maria: postmortem action items already created: add seqlen perf gates, add kernel rollout canary memory checks, make compiler-flag diff mandatory in release notes, and improve streaming fallback behavior.

sre-bot: Note: created alert rule to detect sudden increase in kv-cache host transfers (alert id: SRE-6421).

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 -> mitigated (partial) at 2003456820. Still monitoring.

kevin: final check: global p99 trending down to 700–900ms. Reopen if it regresses.

maria: thanks team. We'll keep this thread open until full rollback finished and fix validated. :thumbsup:

(reacted :eyes: by alex, maria)
